variant_perception_summary: The market prices near-perfect AI capex ROI for Amazon. The engine believes D&A from the $131.8B FY2025 / ~$200B FY2026 capex wave will compress AWS and consolidated margins materially over 18-24 months — a timing mismatch the consensus has not fully priced. However, edge_score = 35 because the D&A lag is directionally known but the magnitude and timing are unresolvable without quarterly D&A disclosure.
what_everyone_knows: AWS is the most profitable segment (35.4% margin, 18% of revenue, 57% of operating income). Amazon is spending $131.8B FY2025 / ~$200B FY2026 on AI infrastructure. E-commerce is the #1 global player. Anthropic is a significant investment.
what_is_priced_in: 16.4% NOPAT CAGR for 10 years (reverse-DCF at $238). Consensus expects ~28% AWS revenue growth and consolidated EBIT expansion from ~$80B to $100B+ by FY2027. Strong balance sheet, AA credit, no near-term distress. Essentially a blue-chip quality premium.
what_market_may_be_missing: D&A billing lag: $131.8B capex in FY2025 (servers, data centres, networking) has a 6-36 month D&A recognition delay. As that arrives in the income statement, Technology & Infrastructure costs will rise, compressing AWS and consolidated margins in FY2026-FY2027. At prior-cycle peak capex ratios, D&A could add $30-50B per year incrementally. Amazon discloses D&A only annually — quarterly transparency is absent — so the market cannot track the compression in real time. Anthropic $60.6B Level 3 mark-to-model inflates GAAP EPS by $2.47/share and cannot be meaningfully valued from public disclosures.
edge_proof: At Q2 2026 earnings (July 31, 2026): if AWS margin compresses more than 150bp year-over-year AND Technology & Infrastructure costs grow faster than revenue, that would confirm the D&A billing-lag hypothesis. Conversely, if AWS margin holds or expands, the hypothesis is wrong and the bull case at $247+ is live. This is the single piece of evidence that would most move conviction in either direction.
killer_risk: D&A from $131.8B FY2025 / ~$200B FY2026 capex wave arrives faster than revenue and compresses AWS margins below 30%, driving EBIT to $60-65B and fair value to $146 or below. Secondary: Anthropic mark-to-model reversal triggers GAAP EPS shock.
